_doc: Move-purity manifest. Each target declares the original file and its replacement PARTS, where every part records the ORIGINAL LINE RANGE it covers. catdiff.js asserts: (A) each part's bytes equal the pristine original's bytes for that range, (B) the ranges tile 1..N with no gap or overlap, (C) concatenating them reproduces the whole original byte-for-byte, (D) for client targets, the <script src> order parsed out of the real 'orderFrom' file equals the parts' ascending line order, and (E) every part's current on-disk sha256 matches a pin in clientPins -- the recoverable guarantee for a part declared modified:true, mirroring serverdiff's [SE]. A part with modified:true is EXPECTED to fail (A)/(C) against pristine and is skipped there by design; (E) is what keeps it honest instead, re-pinned deliberately in the same commit as any intentional change. Order is derived from the real HTML, never trusted from this file -- a disagreement between the two is reported as the bug. Check [5] (scriptblock.js) additionally validates the script block itself.
_lineEndings: This repo has core.autocrlf=true: files are CRLF on disk, LF in git blobs (app.js is 891641 bytes on disk vs 874347 in the blob -- exactly one extra byte per line). RAW byte-identity is MANDATORY for client parts; CRLF->LF is used only as a failure diagnostic and can never produce a PASS.

parts.modifiedReason: Switching from one open ticket straight to another (parent breadcrumb, a linked issue) left the PREVIOUS ticket's rendered content on screen, fully visible and interactive, for the whole fetch of the new one -- fixed by covering it with a loading overlay the moment a switch is detected, dropped once the new issue actually finishes rendering (every early-return path, including a slower-to-fail stale request, clears it correctly without clobbering a newer request's own overlay). First client-side use of `modified: true` in this project -- see [E] in catdiff.js, added specifically to keep this declaration honest via a pinned digest rather than a silent, unrecoverable exception.

conventions.lineCounting: part.from/part.to are SPLIT-ELEMENT indices into pristine content split on newline, NOT newline counts. A file with N newlines yields N+1 split elements, the last being the empty string after the final newline. global-search.js: 476 newlines (wc -l), elements 16819-17295 = 477. Pristine app.js: 17294 newlines / 17295 elements. Sum of wc -l over all 42 client files = 17294. Neither number is wrong -- see AUDIT-FINDINGS.md.
conventions.moves: targets[].moves declares intentional relocations of a block between split files. Contiguity is deliberately broken for the files involved: catdiff [A] becomes move-aware (pristine MINUS blocks moved out, PLUS blocks moved in at the declared position) and [C] becomes REVERSIBILITY -- un-apply every declared move against the files actual bytes and require pristine back line-for-line.
conventions.libPins: lib/ has no pristine original to tile against -- it is hand-written code predating the refactor -- so libdiff.js pins a sha256 per file instead. Any byte change fails [L1] until the pin is updated in the SAME commit with a reason. Unlike serverdiff modified:true, a pin is RESTORED on re-pinning, so lib/ coverage does not decay.

lib/migrations/index.js.note: re-pinned: added 021-dedupe-and-enforce-space-key-uniqueness -- 014 skips silently (and marks itself applied forever) when a spaces.key duplicate already exists at boot, so the DB-level unique index can be permanently missing even after the duplicate is fixed by hand. 021 resolves any existing duplicate (active space keeps the key, archived one is renamed) and creates the index itself if 014 never could -- closes the same TOCTOU race findSpaceKeyConflict alone cannot
